# aeneid-075 drafter notes (X.276–361)

36 units. Title `Tarchonis naufragium. Pugna in litore`; part "The Landing and the Battle on the Shore (X.276–361)".
¶ units: 276, 287, 308.

## Misprints (rule 5b; t kept as printed, l/i corrected)
- 10.298 `semel. ”Quae` for `semel.” Quae`. Handled as aeneid-070: unit 297–298 ends at `semel.` and its l/i
  close Tarchon's speech with ”; the stray ” begins the t of unit 298–302 (5 lines), whose l/i carry no mark.
  Carrying the narrative on instead would have made 294–302 nine lines. Note of 297 opens with the rule-5b sentence.
- 10.335 `campis. ”Tum` for `campis.” Tum`. Same handling: unit 333–335 closes the speech in l/i; the stray ”
  begins the t of unit 335–336 (`”Tum magnam corripit hastam / et iacit:`). Note of 333 opens with the rule-5b sentence.
- No other misprint found (checked for lowercase after a stop and wrong letters).
- make_units.py checks speech-mark balance over each of these two unit pairs instead of unit by unit.

## Doubtful readings / variants
- 10.278 bracketed by Greenough as spurious; kept in [ ] in t, l and i; note of unit 278–279 says so.
- 10.284 half-line, noted (unit 284–286). Its comma inside the closing mark (`iuvat,”`) is kept as printed.
- 10.293 proram/proras: noted (sense: Tarchon's own ship vs the whole fleet).
- 10.307 pedem/pedes: mentioned briefly as no change of sense.
- 10.350 Tres/tris: noted only as Greenough printing both forms in 350–351 (no sense change).

## Attributions written from memory, not checked against a text
- 10.276 almost repeats IX.126; 10.278 repeats IX.127.
- Terence, Phormio 203, `fortis fortuna adiuvat`.
- "More than fifty" half-lines in the Aeneid (usual count given as about 57–58).
- Hector's rally, Iliad 15.494–499 (fight for wife and children).
- Aphrodite rescues Aeneas, Iliad 5.311–318; Athena turns Pandarus's arrow from Menelaus, Iliad 4.127–133.
- Winds simile marked "perhaps": Iliad 16.765–769.
- `haeret pede pes… viro vir` ~ Iliad 13.130–131 and 16.215.
- Children born by caesarean said to be sacred to Apollo (Servius's explanation); Asclepius cut from his dead mother.
- Book VII catalogue: Clausus as founder of the Claudii, Halaesus of Agamemnon's line, Messapus son of Neptune,
  not wounded by fire or steel. Line numbers deliberately not given.
- Tarchon introduced in Book VIII (no line number given).

## For QUESTIONS.md
- 10.284 `Audentis Fortuna iuvat` is a famous tag but not on the set-piece list. Drafted from the Latin as
  l "Those who dare, Fortune helps,”" / i "Fortune lends her help to those who dare,”", avoiding the familiar
  English proverb. Should it become a house rendering?
